sentences.text: The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
Tototlmimus is classified as a medium-sized ornithomimid dinosaur.
This animal possesses a typical ornithomimosaur foot structure known as an arctometatarsus, where the third metatarsal narrows at the top.
The third metatarsal has a weakly developed ginglymoid inferior articular surface.
The foot claws are narrow, asymmetric, and feature shallow grooves on both sides.
The species Tototlmimus packardensis was formally described in October 2015 by Claudia Inés Serrano-Brañas and colleagues.
The holotype specimen ERNO 8553 was found in the Cabullona Group of Sonora, Mexico, and dates to approximately 72 million years ago.
The genus name Tototlmimus is derived from the Nahuatl word for 'bird' and the Latin word for 'mimic'.
The specific name packardensis refers to the fossil's origin in the Packard Formation.
Tototlmimus is classified within the family Ornithomimidae in a derived position.
It is the first named ornithomimid from Mexico and represents one of the southernmost known species in North America.
Cladistic analysis suggests that Tototlmimus is the sister genus to Ornithomimus.
Tototlmimus was an extinct ornithomimid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) in Sonora, Mexico.
The time range for Tototlmimus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
